changes: Separate Emergency Charge phase priority, default EV settings; normal Share follows individual EV grid priorities, not PV share.
One bounded phase/Peak Guard reservation uses permitted EV requests from the existing EV portfolio; existing weighted allocation is reused.
Emergency receives minimum-current start capacity before extra charging; only battery charging limits are reduced, with no new battery ramp.
EV preparation preserves at least the battery charging needed to keep measured grid import non-negative, including command quantization.
A start needs measured phase and total Peak Guard room; a battery Flow receipt is not confirmation.
Unconfirmed/failed EV output and battery/Split output cannot create fictitious capacity on a new P1 packet.
Reservations cancel/expire on existing evaluation moments; partial failed EV starts retain conservative safety accounting for at most the existing 60-second feedback horizon.
Immediate full permissible battery restoration remains subject to existing command intervals and safety limits.

user_clarifications.order: Reduce battery first only where this does not create export, wait for measured capacity, then EV minimum start.
user_clarifications.zero_total_grid: Zero total import alone is not a guarantee of per-phase room or sufficient total Peak Guard capacity. PV absorption is retained until actual EV consumption creates room.
user_clarifications.obsolete_tests: User authorized removing obsolete fixed-50/50 expectations from three test files. Other feedback/publication/safety assertions are retained; fixtures explicitly select EV grid sharing where that sharing is part of the scenario.

remaining_limits: All I/O tests are simulated; no Homey installation/publication or physical EV/battery test was performed.
Fresh complete phase readings and reliable EV current feedback are required. Single-phase EV location and unknown battery phase mappings remain conservative.
A transient caused by hardware response, external load changes or delayed input is handled by existing safety paths; software/Flow commands are not certified instantaneous electrical protection.
A start that would require preparation-induced export, exceed a phase limit/Peak Guard, or interfere with necessary Safety SoC restoration must wait.
